title: Make Array Non-decreasing or Non-increasing
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, determine the least number of operations needed to make the array either non-decreasing or non-increasing.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, determine the least number of operations needed to make the array either non-decreasing or non-increasing. An operation consists of selecting an index i (0 <= i < nums.length) and incrementing or decrementing nums[i] by 1.
constraints: One operation increments or decrements one element by one.
The final array may be either non-decreasing or non-increasing.
Return the minimum total number of unit changes; values need not remain within the original range during operations.
hints: Solve the non-decreasing direction with a max-heap, then solve non-increasing by reversing the input.
When the greatest prior adjusted value exceeds the current value, lower that maximum to the current value and add the difference.
Push each value; on a violation pop the heap maximum, add maximum-current, and push current again.
The heap maintains an optimal multiset of adjusted prefix values; replacing its largest violation is the minimum local repair and the standard isotonic L1 exchange argument makes it globally optimal.
editorial: The heap maintains an optimal multiset of adjusted prefix values; replacing its largest violation is the minimum local repair and the standard isotonic L1 exchange argument makes it globally optimal.

tests.explanation: The cheapest monotone adjustment uses four unit changes.
Changing the final one to three costs two and makes the array non-decreasing.
